reasoning: The claim is fully supported by established biological facts and marine science sources. Octopuses possess three hearts: two branchial hearts that pump blood through the gills, and one systemic heart that circulates blood to the rest of the body. Furthermore, octopus blood is blue because it relies on hemocyanin, a copper-rich protein that transports oxygen, unlike the iron-rich hemoglobin found in human red blood cells.
